LMP3.title: RLR’s fuel-saving Ligier wins the LMP3 opener
LMP3.dek: Van Uitert, Farano and Garofall won the opening LMP3 round for RLR MSport, leading almost throughout on fuel-saving strategy, with the pole-sitting M.Racing Norma second.

facts.v: The #15 Ligier gave RLR MSport its first class win since Imola 2015 and was the 12th ELMS victory for the Ligier JS P3.

chapters.title: Eighteen cars and a row over Silvers
text: Eighteen LMP3 cars started the 2018 season, mostly Ligier JS P3s but with four Norma M30s in the field. The newest Norma was Ultimate’s, delivered only days before the Paul Ricard Prologue; the team kept its Ligier as well but did not plan to run it anywhere else. United Autosports arrived as the defending class champions with the #2 of Falb and Rayhall, a car that lost track time in the Prologue to two driveshaft failures on the Monday.

The talking point of the paddock was the #8 DKR Engineering Norma. Glorieux and Alex Toril, who had won the Michelin Le Mans Cup together in 2017, were joined by Alex’s brother Miguel, and all three were Silver-rated, outside the usual championship line-up rules. The organisers had accepted the entry on condition that it gained no competitive advantage, a premise most rival teams rejected, and DKR did little to calm things by topping two Prologue sessions, with a best of 1:51.363.

Elsewhere the class had plenty of new faces. Ecurie Ecosse/Nielsen’s #7 paired Kapadia and Noble with Christian Olsen, a bronze-rated newcomer from historic Formula 3 making his first sportscar season, and Inter Europol’s #14 had Enqvist in place of Molinaro. Practice at Paul Ricard began in light rain, and RLR’s van Uitert led the final session on 1:52.290 from United’s #3 and Eurointernational’s #11.

chapters.title: Droux takes the first pole for M.Racing
text: The ten-minute session was interrupted by a red flag when Senna stopped the United LMP2 Ligier on the Mistral Straight, and the LMP3 order stayed very tight, with the top three inside a tenth of each other after a flurry of late improvements. Droux put the #19 M.Racing - YMR Norma on pole with 1:51.930, the first ELMS pole for the Yvan Muller-led team.

Van Uitert had briefly held provisional pole for RLR, and was 0.045s behind Droux’s final time, but his fastest lap was deleted for a track-limits infringement and the #15 slipped to fourth. That promoted Lahaye’s Ultimate Norma #17 to second, 0.061s off pole, and the #8 DKR Norma to third on 1:52.104. The quickest United was the #2 in fifth, seven tenths off pole, with Bell’s #3 sixth and Kaiser’s 360 Racing #6 seventh.

chapters.title: RLR hit the front, Ultimate and DKR lose out
text: Van Uitert, in his first ELMS start, undid the qualifying deletion quickly. He pushed hard from the start, took the lead of the class soon afterwards and handed a leading Ligier over to Farano. Behind him two of the pre-race favourites lost their races early. Ultimate’s #17 came in with an electronic problem on lap 11 and spent almost an hour in the garage, and DKR’s #8 was out when Glorieux went off and could not restart the car.

chapters.title: A lead that never really came under threat
text: The safety car period just before halfway, triggered by the LMP2 DragonSpeed and a Spirit of Race Ferrari colliding at Signes, brought the field together but did not take the lead from RLR, whose #15 ran at the front almost throughout. Its team chose a strategy built around saving fuel, with Farano and then Garofall driving the stints behind van Uitert’s opening run. Only two cars were really in a position to fight it: Eurointernational’s #11 of Mondini and van Berlo, and the #19 shared by Légeret, Droux and Ferrer.

chapters.title: Garofall holds the gap, the Norma takes second
text: With 45 minutes left Garofall had more than 20 seconds in hand over van Berlo in the #11 and Légeret in the #19, and he held the gap to the flag, even as the team worried about running dry and prepared for a splash-and-dash that proved unnecessary. The pole-sitting Norma took second place in the final half hour and finished about 32 seconds behind the winner, with the Eurointernational Ligier a further 19 seconds back in third. Woodward and Kaiser’s 360 Racing Ligier was just off the podium in fourth.

chapters.title: RLR’s first win since Imola 2015
text: The #15 RLR MSport Ligier of van Uitert, Farano and Garofall won on 119 laps, giving the British team its first class win since Imola 2015, Garofall’s second in LMP3 and the 12th ELMS victory for the Ligier JS P3. Van Uitert said he had pushed hard in his first stint and that Garofall’s closing stint was perfect, while Farano praised the team’s strategy call. Van Uitert also set the class fastest lap, 1:52.941.

M.Racing - YMR’s #19 was second and Eurointernational’s #11 third, both on the winner’s lap, with the #6 360 Racing Ligier fourth. United’s #2 was classified fifth. Inter Europol’s #13 led the cars on 118 laps in sixth, ahead of United’s #3, AT Racing’s #9 and Ecurie Ecosse/Nielsen’s #7. Only the #17 Ultimate Norma and the #8 DKR Norma were not classified. The series moves on to Monza on 13 May.

LMGTE.title: Molina’s last-lap pass gives JMW Ferrari the win over Proton Porsche
LMGTE.dek: Griffin, MacDowall and Molina won for JMW after Molina passed Proton’s Cairoli on the final lap, with EbiMotors third as Gulf and Spirit of Race’s #55 retired.

facts.t: Only the last lap in front
facts.v: JMW’s Ferrari led the class for just one lap of the four hours, the last, and the win was the team’s first since Le Mans 2017.

chapters.title: Proton’s damaged Porsches and a guest from the WEC
text: Eight GTE cars lined up for the opening round, four Ferrari 488 GTEs and four Porsche 911 RSRs, and the build-up was dominated by the state of the Porsches. Proton Competition’s brand-new #77 was heavily damaged at Turn 3 in the first Prologue session, and Joel Camathias, who had been due to share it with Ried and Olsen, parted company with the team a few days later. Dienst, who had driven for Proton in the WEC, took his seat, and the team reverted to one of its WEC-spec chassis. EbiMotors, running a repurposed ex-WEC Proton chassis as the #80 until its own car arrived after Le Mans, had its own Prologue crash when Babini hit the barriers, but the car was repaired in time for the second day.

JMW Motorsport arrived as defending champions with the #66 Ferrari, Krohn Racing’s Tracy Krohn and Jönsson returned to the series, and Gulf Racing UK entered a Porsche as a guest from the WEC. Gulf skipped the Prologue, so its first run on the ELMS GTE Dunlops came in Friday’s first session. In that damp session Cairoli’s #88 Proton was quickest on 2:01.282, with Gulf’s Barker two tenths back and Dienst third on his first run in the #77. In the final practice the #88 led again on 1:54.253, with the #77 second and Gulf less than a tenth further back, and the best Ferrari was Spirit of Race’s #55.

chapters.title: Cairoli on pole, Gulf thrown to the back
text: Cairoli took pole for Proton with a 1:53.377 on his first flying lap, in a quiet session for the eight cars in the class. It was the team’s seventh ELMS pole, a record, and the first with the new 911 RSR; Cairoli said he had not been feeling well. Barker had set the benchmark at the start of the session for Gulf with 1:53.586 and could not improve, which left the Porsche on the front row until the stewards deleted all of its times after the session because its rear diffuser breached Article 12 of the technical regulations. Gulf started from the back of the grid.

That promoted JMW’s #66 to second, with Molina’s 1:54.562 more than a second off the pole time. Olsen put the #77 Proton Porsche next on 1:54.830, then came Krohn’s #83 (Bertolini, 1:54.905), Spirit of Race’s #55 (Matt Griffin, 1:54.949), EbiMotors’ #80 (Pera, 1:55.183) and Spirit of Race’s #54 (Castellacci, 1:55.790).

chapters.title: Wainwright drives through from the back
text: With the Gulf Porsche at the back of the grid, Wainwright produced an excellent opening stint and carved through the class, setting up the fight to the front that his team-mate Barker took on later. Ahead of them the #88 Proton of Cairoli and the Rodas took up the pace-setting, and it led most of the four hours.

chapters.title: Attrition thins the class
text: The Gulf Porsche, which had climbed to the front and led for a short spell, was out after 45 laps with mechanical problems. Shortly before halfway DragonSpeed’s LMP2 Oreca driven by Hedman collided with Spirit of Race’s #55 Ferrari at the fast Signes right-hander, taking both cars out and bringing out a safety car. With the Gulf and the #55 gone, EbiMotors’ debutant Porsche, which had been in the mix for a podium all along, moved into a secure third place. The Rodas and Cairoli were almost untouchable in the #88, but their comfortable lead started to disappear as the race entered its final hour.

chapters.title: Molina takes it on the last lap
text: In the last hour Molina chased down a gap of about 14 seconds in the JMW Ferrari and arrived on Cairoli’s tail in the closing minutes. The Porsche started the final lap in front, but Molina put the Ferrari up the inside, the two cars banging doors, and took the lead. Cairoli pushed hard for the rest of the lap through the traffic, but could not find a way back past, and Molina held on to win. The last lap was the only lap of the race JMW had led. Liam Griffin said the team had been written off early, and that they thought the flag had already been shown before the last lap, so they were slow to realise what was happening.

chapters.title: JMW win, EbiMotors on the podium
text: The #66 JMW Ferrari of Liam Griffin, MacDowall and Molina won on 118 laps, the team’s first victory since Le Mans in 2017 and the start of a championship lead for the 2017 title winners. Gianluca Roda, Giorgio Roda Jr and Cairoli finished second for Proton in the #88, on the same lap, and Babini, Pera and Narac took third in the #80 EbiMotors Porsche on its series debut, one lap down. Molina set the fastest lap of the class, 1:54.670, with Cairoli next on 1:54.888.

Krohn Racing’s #83 Ferrari was fourth, a good result for Krohn and Jönsson’s return, ahead of Proton’s #77 in fifth and Spirit of Race’s #54 in sixth, 11 laps behind the winner. The #55 and the Gulf Porsche #86 were not classified. The series next goes to Monza on 13 May.
